channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Spring 2027 SFW Resident Artist Program — SERVICE · Kent Cultural Alliance
item.description: A six-week live-in, work-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland on the theme of SERVICE — work made to serve the needs of the communities it is made for. The session runs March 14 to April 24, 2027, in partnership with For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall; three artists are selected. Each receives a $7,500 stipend, travel reimbursement up to $1,000 and studio and gallery expense reimbursement up to $1,500, with accommodation at the Vincent & Leslie Prince Raimond Cultural Center, a 1799 building the National Park Service has selected as an escape site on its Network to Freedom. Community engagement is the cornerstone: residents are embedded with a local partner organisation for the first week, then have five weeks to make finished or substantially finished work, alongside one or two workshops with a local social-service agency or school, an open studio Saturday and two or three evening presentations. Work is exhibited in KCA's 1,000 sq ft gallery after an opening reception on the final Friday of the session; artists may sell, and KCA takes no commission and does not broker. There is no fee to apply, but the application is more than a form: two required narrative statements of 500 words or less — one on the link between your work and community engagement, one on your connection to the theme of SERVICE — plus up to 4 images of current work and links to a website and/or social media. Photography is not named as a category, but the application form states that 'all disciplines of artistry are encouraged including visual art, creative writing, music, fashion, dance, etc.' — an open list. Eligibility is post-degree career artists based in the USA; international artists only with a current visa permitting legal work in the USA (no tourist visas); no current degree candidates. The residency cannot accommodate children, families or pets; the building is fully accessible and includes an ADA-compliant bedroom. Deadline is December 1, 2026 at 5:00 pm EST — a 5 pm cutoff, not midnight. A second open call for the Fall 2027 session is expected. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $7,500 stipend + up to $1,000 travel + up to $1,500 studio and gallery expenses + six-week gallery exhibition.

item.title: Industry, Labor, and Community AIR 2027 · WVU Libraries
item.description: WVU Libraries' Art in the Libraries Program invites artists to work with the Industry, Labor, and Community collections at the West Virginia & Regional History Center — union records, company-town archives, oral histories and grassroots community papers — and make new work from them. The 2027 cycle's theme is Common Threads: Industry, Labor & Community. Photography is explicitly in the accepted media list, and the organiser's own examples name a 'Photographic Series' responding to archival images. The award is $1,000 for materials paid on signing, up to $3,500 in reimbursement for transportation, lodging and per diem, and a $1,000 honorarium on completion. The residency is a 5–7 day stay in Morgantown in March or April 2027, including at least two full days in the WVRHC archives, followed by a public programme and exhibition launch at the WVU Downtown Library in April 2027 and a 20-minute community presentation. Ownership of the finished work remains entirely with the artist. Juried by the WVU Art in the Libraries Committee with WVRHC archivists and guest juror Rachel Johnson of the Morgantown Arts Council. Proposals that highlight underrepresented narratives, elevate local working-class history or explore the human impact of regional industry are given strong consideration, and WVU alumni and underrepresented artists are especially encouraged. Note that the page states its geography twice and differently: the programme description says 'open to all U.S. and Canadian-based artists' while the Application Process block, which governs, says 'based in the United States'. Apply by emailing a single combined PDF (abstract, statement of interest, timeline and budget, artist statement, 2-page CV, 5–10 images or web links) to the curator. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 materials + up to $3,500 travel, lodging and per diem + $1,000 honorarium + exhibition at WVU Downtown Library.

item.title: Fall 2027 - Spring 2028 Solo Exhibitions · SRO Photo Gallery, Texas Tech University
item.description: SRO Photo Gallery is a graduate-student-run exhibition space inside the Digital and Narrative Arts program at the Texas Tech University School of Art, and its annual open call programmes a whole academic year: six to eight solo exhibitions of still photographic work plus four solo moving-image exhibitions, shown between August 2027 and May 2028. A solo slot, not a group hang. Submission is free and goes by email, with no platform in between. Two physical constraints are worth reading before you apply, because they shape what can be shown: prints are displayed unframed — matted, loose, or mounted on thin backing — inside eight glass display cases measuring 30 x 72 x 1 inches each, and moving image work is shown on four wall-mounted monitors side by side (.MOV, .MPG and MPEG-4 only), so video applicants are asked for four 2-5 minute teasers from the same project. Still-image applicants send a PDF slideshow of 20 images at 2000 pixels on the long edge, with title, medium, dimensions and year, plus a bio or CV and an artist or project statement carrying full contact details. Portfolios are reviewed by a committee of Digital & Narrative Arts faculty and students together with the Landmark Arts staff; the gallery asks for lens-based work in any style, technique or aesthetic approach, and says consistency in the work, as well as creative vision, is what weighs in the selection process. The deadline is published as a bare date with no time of day and no timezone on either of the two pages that carry it, and 28 March 2027 falls on a Sunday, so treat the Friday before as the working cutoff. Selected artists are announced in early May 2027 and are reproduced in a full-colour brochure published annually and distributed locally and nationally. The call carries no entry fee and no cash prize. — Deadline: March 28, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + printed brochure.

item.title: PhotoNOLA PhotoBOOK Prize 2026 · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: The New Orleans Photo Alliance's third annual photobook prize, decided around the PhotoNOLA PhotoBOOK Fair at the historic Patrick F. Taylor Library inside the Ogden Museum of Southern Art — Saturday 5 December 2026, 11am–4pm, inside the 21st PhotoNOLA festival (2–6 December). Open to any artist who has published a photobook in the past five years, with self-published titles explicitly welcomed and encouraged. Two cautions, both measured on the page itself: it gives the eligibility window twice and the two disagree — the guidelines say December 2021 to December 2026, while the entry form's own publication-date field still says "Book must be published between December 2020 and December 2025", which is last year's wording carried over. And its single deadline sentence reads "Sunday, November 13th, 11:59pm" with no year, but 13 November 2026 is a Friday; we store the earlier of the two readings, so treat Friday the 13th as the cutoff and do not count on the 15th. The Grand Prize is $500 plus a Silver NOPA membership; an Award of Excellence and a Louisiana Award of Excellence — the latter reserved for a Louisiana resident, who is also considered for all three prizes — each carry a Silver membership. All three winners are offered the chance to be included at the 2026 Photobook Prize table at the 2027 PhotoNOLA PhotoWALK and Photobook Fair; the page words that as an opportunity, not a guarantee. You enter the book itself through the form on PhotoNOLA's own page: a PDF of the whole volume and a description of up to 600 words are required, a photograph of the book is optional. No juror is named. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $500 + NOPA membership + fair table.

item.title: In The Abstract 2027 — Virtual Exhibition · San Fernando Valley Arts & Cultural Center
item.description: SFVACC's annual abstract-art open call, in its virtual edition: a juried online exhibition running 24 February to 30 April 2027. The geography is worth reading twice before paying: the prospectus body says the show "is open to all artists" and the CaFE record's location bucket reads International, but the binding Eligibility Criteria field on the same page narrows it — "In The Abstract a Virtual Exhibition is open to all artists residing in North America." Outside the US, Canada or Mexico, ask SFVACC before entering. The brief is the broad one — "Abstract art uses shapes, forms, color, line and texture as opposed to representing an accurate depiction of visual reality" — and the organiser says it "seeks artists who can provide a well-rounded range of 2D and 3D abstract art." Photographers are in scope on the prospectus's own terms: up to six original works per artist, submitted as JPEGs, "in all media except video." Juror Genie Davis, a writer, art curator and the owner of Diversions Fine Arts Gallery in Manhattan Beach, selects an $800 Best of Show (plus a listing on SFVACC's Best of Show page), $400 first place, $300 second place and up to four Honorable Mentions. Entry is $40 for the first work with up to five more at $5 each, and SFVACC is running an early-bird code (SaveVirtual) that takes $10 off until 30 November 2026. The sales terms are unusually clean for an online show: buyers contact the artist directly through the exhibition page, SFVACC takes no commission at all, and prices are fixed at the figure given at submission. Three conditions to read first: work made under an instructor's direct supervision is not eligible, a submitted work cannot be substituted or withdrawn, and work previously shown in any SFVACC exhibit should not be entered. Accepted work stays online until the exhibition closes. Entries close 24 January 2027 at 11:59pm PST, with acceptances emailed by 31 January. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $40 ($30 with early-bird code until Nov 30), $5 each additional. Prize: $800 / $400 / $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: In The Abstract 2027 — In-Person Exhibition · San Fernando Valley Arts & Cultural Center
item.description: The gallery half of SFVACC's annual abstract open call: a juried show at TAG Gallery, 5458 Wilshire Boulevard in Los Angeles, running 24 February to 19 March 2027. The theme is abstraction broadly understood — "shapes, forms, color, line and texture as opposed to representing an accurate depiction of visual reality" — and the organiser asks for "a well-rounded range of 2D and 3D abstract art." Photography qualifies on the prospectus's own wording — up to six original works per artist, juried from JPEGs — but this edition carries format bars the virtual one does not: "No AI. No Video. No giclee prints.", a 30-inch maximum in every direction including the frame for wall work, 2D work wired and ready to hang, and "Only plexiglass on 2D work. No glass!" If your prints are pigment inkjet, put the giclée line to SFVACC before paying — the organiser does not define the term. Juror Genie Davis, writer, curator and owner of Diversions Fine Arts Gallery in Manhattan Beach, picks an $800 Best of Show plus a listing on SFVACC's Best of Show page, $400 first place, $300 second place and up to four Honorable Mentions, announced at the opening reception. The hard constraint is delivery: artists must hand-deliver and collect the work themselves at TAG Gallery, on set dates in February and March, and no shipped artwork is accepted at all — which in practice limits this edition to artists who can get to Los Angeles. Commercial terms are specific too: all accepted work must be for sale, priced at $250 or more, TAG Gallery takes 35% of any sale and pays the artist 65% about 60 days after the show closes, while SFVACC takes nothing. Work made under an instructor's direct supervision is not eligible, a submitted work cannot be substituted or withdrawn, and work already shown in an SFVACC exhibit should not be entered. Entry is $40 for the first piece and $5 for each of up to five more; entries close 24 January 2027 at 11:59pm PST with acceptances emailed by 31 January. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $40 first entry, $5 each additional. Prize: $800 / $400 / $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: E Pluribus: From Many · Latino Arts, Inc.
item.description: Latino Arts marks forty years of programmes rooted in "Cultura y Corazón: Culture and Heart" with a juried exhibition at its Milwaukee gallery, 5 March to 4 June 2027, made with the Milwaukee Institute of Art & Design and the Richard and Ethel Herzfeld Foundation. E Pluribus means "from many," and the show is about how many voices, histories and traditions can sit together while staying distinct: work is invited through personal, cultural, community-based or cross-cultural perspectives on the mix of cultures, practices and lived experiences that shape Hispanic and Latino identities. The call is open to artists from within the Latino/Hispanic community and to artists who are allies of it through their practice, and the organiser is explicit about how that is read — "The process does not ask whether a work is Hispanic or Latino enough." Applicants must be 18 or over and live in Wisconsin, Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois or Michigan. Up to two original works per artist, no collaborations, completed in 2025 or later, nothing that has already won an award in another juried show, and the work must be two-dimensional, within 6ft high by 8ft wide by 2in deep — which photographs satisfy on the organiser's own criterion. "Digital art is welcome, though strictly NO AI generated images will be allowed." Artists choose one of two tracks for both submissions, Emerging or Established, each defined by practice rather than by age, schooling or sales: the Jurors' Choice recognition is $1,000 in the Established track and $800 in the Emerging one. Required with every entry, beyond the images: an artist statement of 100–250 words and a biography of no more than 150 words. One content rule applies to the work itself — it "must not contain explicit language or sexual imagery." Entry is $40 per artwork, so two works cost $80. Selected artists arrange delivery and transport of the work to the Milwaukee gallery themselves, on set dates in late February 2027. Submissions opened 30 October 2026 and close Sunday 10 January 2027 at 11:59pm CST, with selection notices on 20 January. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: $40 per artwork. Prize: $1,000 / $800 + Exhibition.

item.title: Read This · Fine Line Creative Arts Center
item.description: A Kavanagh Gallery show about text in art, at Fine Line Creative Arts Center in the Fox River Valley about an hour west of Chicago, running 27 May to 9 July 2027. The organiser's framing is deliberately wide: "Combining text with imagery has a long history in art that continues to grow. Artists use text in paintings, prints, and other 2-dimensional art forms, as well as carved and stamped into 3-dimensional sculptures, pottery, and glass. Whether the text is with or without literal meaning, hidden within the piece or clearly visible, the work must contain text as part of the composition." That is the only constraint on subject, and the media bar is simply "All media will be accepted" — which makes it an open door for photographers working with signage, letterforms, handwriting, documents or any image that carries words. $800 in prizes will be awarded; the judge is listed as to be determined. Open to any artist 18 or older resident in the United States, up to three pieces for a single non-refundable $35 entry, one entry per artist, with selections made from the submitted images on creativity, quality of artistry and originality. Two required items are easy to miss: an artist statement of no more than 1,000 characters that "must not include the artist’s name", and a sale price on every piece — "Artwork on an application without a sale price will not move to the jury phase." Three practical conditions are worth pricing before entering: the artist pays shipping to and from Fine Line and must include a return label, the artist insures the work in transit (Fine Line deems the insurance value to be 70% of the sale price), and because this is a selling gallery show all accepted work must be for sale with a 30% commission on anything sold — Fine Line handles the sales and sales tax and pays out after the show closes. Applications are due 12 April 2027, jury decisions go out by email on 23 April, and work is delivered and checked in on 22 May 2027. — Deadline: April 12, 2027. Fee: $35/3 works. Prize: $800 in prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: The Last Supper (The Last Casa Bonita Art Show) · NEXT Gallery
item.description: The tenth and final edition of NEXT Gallery's Casa Bonita Art Show, and the brief is gloriously specific: "ALL SUBMISSIONS MUST DIRECTLY RELATE TO THE CASA BONITA RESTAURANT IN LAKEWOOD, COLORADO" — the place with an 85-foot pink stucco tower, a 30-foot indoor waterfall, cliff divers, mariachi, puppet shows and a haunted cave. This year's theme is The Last Supper, which the gallery is careful to frame as "a jumping off point, not a religious assignment. Think: meals, indulgences, gatherings, futures, pasts, endings, chances… The interpretation is up to you." A national juried call, open to all, one work per entry; alongside visual art the gallery is taking literary submissions on the same theme (flash fiction to 400 words, poetry to one page, previously published work accepted with permission). Cash prizes and Casa Bonita swag will be awarded, though no figures are published. Jurors are Casa Bonita Art Show founder Dolla B, Casa Bonita aficionado Andrew Novick and fashion designer Mona Lucero. The show runs 12 to 28 February 2027 at NEXT Gallery in the 40 West Arts Hub in Lakewood, with accepted work dropped off on 7 or 8 February and mailed work received by 8 February; out-of-state artists make specific arrangements with the gallery. Sold work carries a 33% commission and prices cannot be changed after acceptance. AI is barred twice over: "No AI Art will be accepted" in the eligibility criteria and "Absolutely NO AI/ChatGPT work will be considered" for the literary half. Entry is $35, or $15 for entrants under 13, and closes at midnight MST on 18 January 2027. — Deadline: January 18, 2027. Fee: $35 ($15 under 13). Prize: Cash prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: The Winter Show 2026 · Palos Verdes Art Center
item.description: Palos Verdes Art Center's members-only winter group show, juried for its Main Gallery on the Palos Verdes peninsula and hanging 4 December 2026 to 9 January 2027. It is an all-media call with no theme, and photography is squarely in scope — the organiser's own submission instructions ask artists to "identify your media and substrate; for instance, oil on canvas, digital print on paper, etc." The juror is Carrie Burckle, a Los Angeles artist, educator and curator, founding member and Executive Director of Textile Arts LA and for twenty-plus years adjunct faculty in the Fiber program at CSULB, with work shown at the Craft and Folk Art Museum and Craft in America Center in Los Angeles, Visions Art Museum and Mingei Museum in San Diego, and the Collins Gallery in Glasgow. Up to three pieces for a $35 entry, one image per artwork, JPEGs at 1,200 pixels or more on the longest side, nothing previously exhibited at PVAC, maximum size 50 by 60 inches including the frame. Two things are required beyond the fee: entrants must be a current PVAC member in good standing (individual membership is $50 a year, family $60), and selected work must be hand-delivered to the Main Gallery on Friday 20 November between 9 and 11am — "No early deliveries. All work must be delivered on November 20, 2026" — with pick-up on 11 January. There is no cash award of any kind; the opportunity is the show itself, plus a selling wall at a 25% commission. PVAC insures work for the duration of the exhibition only and carries no earthquake insurance. Submissions opened 16 October and close 2 November 2026; the juror's selections are announced through CaFE in November — the prospectus gives two dates for that, "Tuesday, November 10, 2026" in its calendar and "by November 5" in its selection block. PVAC's own website carries no page for this edition: its exhibitions index lists The Winter Show 2025 as the newest, and its Winter Show call route still shows the 2023–24 edition with a different juror, so the CaFE listing is the only current surface. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: $35 (PVAC membership required, $50/year individual). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 58th Annual Summer Arts Festival Poster Contest · Umpqua Valley Arts
item.description: Umpqua Valley Arts has run a poster contest for its Summer Arts Festival since the festival began, and the 58th edition is open: the winning image becomes the face of the whole event. There is no theme. UVA asks for work that embodies the spirit of the festival — a gathering of artists, food vendors and entertainers — and says reflecting Douglas County or Central Oregon is welcome but optional, adding that it "welcomes artwork that represents the artist's own style/subject matter of choice." The entry form's own rule is the binding one: "Open to all artists to submit up to (3) entries of two dimensional artwork/s. Open media." Both traditional and digital work are accepted, and the only format bar is that the work be two-dimensional and reproducible — photographs qualify on the organiser's own terms, with files wanted as JPEGs at 300dpi, 1920px on the longest side. A panel of UVA staff with local art professionals and community representatives judges from the digital files on craftsmanship, creative ability, ingenuity and design. The winner receives a $500 prize, a free Summer Arts Festival T-shirt, free entry to the festival, credit on the poster itself and credit in the visitor guide; the selected artwork is then converted to a digital file and used across the festival's website, social media, posters, apparel, postcards, programme, press releases and signage, and may be slightly altered, cropped or edited to fit those formats and carry festival information. Two clauses are worth reading before entering: the rules reserve UVA the right to reproduce or edit artwork from the submitted digital images for publicity purposes, and an accepted work cannot be substituted or withdrawn. AI tools are barred outright — the criteria require that "the work is not created with the use of AI programs or tools." Entry is free and closes 12 December 2026, and the form does name a notification window: the winner "will be selected and will be contacted directly by late December 2026." — Deadline: December 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500.

item.title: 37th Annual Dayton Works on Paper · Rosewood Arts Center
item.description: Rosewood Arts Center, the City of Kettering's arts facility just outside Dayton, Ohio, runs its 37th Annual Dayton Works on Paper, a juried exhibition “created for artists living within a 40-mile radius of Dayton, Ohio” — a radius the centre's own prospectus notes “excludes Columbus and Cincinnati”. The show “features two-and three-dimensional works of art on or of paper”, so the support rather than the medium is the test and a photographic print on paper qualifies. The organiser says so itself in its last published prospectus (2025, the 35th annual): “Entries must be original works in any medium on or of paper”. This edition's entry form asks each entrant to type the “Medium of Work” as free text and names no accepted or excluded media, and photographers have been selected repeatedly — a Dayton landscape photographer's CV records selection at the 32nd, 33rd and 34th Annual, “1 of 60 selected from 241 prints” at the 34th, and a Merit Award at the 32nd. The juror distributes “artist awards totaling $1,100”, and gallery visitors choose a People's Choice Award funded through the Joan W. McCoy Memorial Art Fund. The juror for this edition is not named on the organiser's page. Entering is a two-part, in-person process rather than an upload: you complete the Works on Paper 2027 Digital Entry Form (one form covers all three works, asking title, year, medium, dimensions, insurance value and price for each), then bring the physical work and the printed Entry Form/Prospectus to Rosewood Arts Center, 2655 Olson Drive, Kettering, on Saturday 2 January 2027 (the page prints both 12pm–3pm and 1–3pm for this slot) or Monday 4 January 2027, 12–8pm. The entry fee is $20 for up to three artworks. The 2027 prospectus is not online — the page says it can be collected at Rosewood or at playkettering.org/gallery, and it is not on that page today — and the 2025 one carried conditions this edition's page does not repeat: jurying from the actual work rather than from files, a 40-inch width cap without the frame, work completed within the last four years, and nothing previously exhibited at the Gallery. Jury results go out by email by 9pm on Monday 11 January 2027; declined work is collected 12–16 January; the exhibition runs 19 January – 27 February 2027 with a closing reception on Saturday 27 February, and exhibiting work is picked up after the reception or on Monday 1 March, 12–8pm. Work is offered for sale and the price you enter must include the City of Kettering's 30% commission. Every entrant ticks agreement to the Rosewood Gallery Group Exhibition Agreement, a four-page contract linked from the entry form, and it is worth reading before you enter: the artist arranges, pays for and insures framing, packing, shipping and delivery in both directions; Rosewood covers damage only while the work is on display, to a maximum of $20,000; and work left more than fifteen calendar days after the exhibition closes becomes “Abandoned Artwork”, which waives the artist's Visual Artists Rights Act rights of attribution and integrity and transfers ownership to the City, which may then sell, alter or destroy it. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: $20 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,100 in awards + People's Choice Award + Exhibition.

item.title: Open Call — New Perspectives · New & Abstract Gallery Berlin
item.description: New & Abstract, the Berlin gallery that began in 2019 as an Instagram platform and has since shown over a hundred artists across roughly 100 square metres in the centre of the city, is looking for “distinctive, innovative, and exciting artistic positions” on the theme of New Perspectives — “fresh, individual ways of seeing”. The media list is wide and names photography explicitly, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, digital art, sculpture, installation, wall objects and mixed media: “whether figurative or abstract, minimalist or expressive, conceptual or intuitive — surprise us with your unique artistic vision”. Thirty artists are selected for a curated group exhibition at the gallery, running 4–18 December 2026, and receive a feature on the New & Abstract Instagram account, professional photographs of the exhibition, and joint promotion through the gallery’s website, social channels and invitation materials. An independent jury then picks one winner from those thirty for a solo exhibition at the gallery in spring/summer 2027, with the gallery taking care of the concept, communications and opening reception, plus a production grant of up to €500; the winner is announced publicly at the 4 December opening, where attendance is “strongly encouraged but is not a requirement for winning”. Twenty honourable mentions are featured on the gallery’s Instagram feed and stories. The call is “open to artists aged 18 and over from anywhere in the world”; one image is uploaded per application, work for the group show must not exceed 80 × 80 cm, and you must be the creator and rights holder. Practicalities worth pricing in: a non-refundable €20 processing fee applies per artwork submitted, and the gallery states that “no additional costs will arise — not even if you are selected for the exhibition, the online gallery, or Instagram promotion”; the artist keeps 60% of any sale price and is responsible for getting work to Berlin and arranging its return. Jury selection is on engagement with the theme, artistic originality, quality and coherence, and the potential of the practice to grow into an independent solo show. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: €20 per artwork. Prize: Solo exhibition + €500 production grant + Group exhibition.

item.title: What Are You Worried About? · Pajaro Valley Arts
item.description: Pajaro Valley Arts, the Watsonville nonprofit, invites “artists living and/or working in the greater Bay Area” to an invitational and juried exhibition curated by journalist and artist Lillian Schroth. The brief is the worry itself: “Whatever keeps you up at night has a place in this show” — from money, relationships, kids, insomnia, anxiety and “paranoia about what other people think” out to “your city, your country, or the world — AI, the economy, wealth inequality, immigrant rights … climate change, the wars in Gaza, Ukraine and Iran”. PVA states “all genres — and worries — accepted” and “we welcome all art forms and mediums”, listing painting, sculpture, collage, video, audio and writing, so a photographer enters on the same footing as any other medium; each entrant also writes a short description of how the work connects to the theme, and that text hangs with the work if selected. Entry takes up to 4 JPEGs of work new to PVA (no larger than 300 dpi and 6” in any direction, filenames as surname plus title), with writing capped at 300 words and audio or video at 3 minutes for the submission — a selected time-based work may run longer. The calendar is published in full: jurors review 1–15 December, artists are notified on 17 December 2026, loan agreements are due 23 December, work is delivered to Watsonville on 26 January 2027, and the show runs 9 February – 13 March 2027 with a reception on Saturday 13 February, 1–3pm. THE COSTS: there is no entry fee, but “upon acceptance/selection into the exhibit, there is a $35.00 participation fee for each artist, to be paid with the submittal of the loan agreement”, which PVA says “helps offset exhibit expenses” while noting “some participation sponsorships may be available” — ask if the fee is a barrier. Sales commission is 30% for PVA members and 50% for non-members, and the page asks for membership “in good standing through March 13, 2026” (the organiser’s own date, which sits a year before this exhibition closes). Delivery is the artist’s own job and PVA states “we are unable to accept artwork through the mail for this exhibit”, so entering means getting the work to Watsonville in person (or by a representative) in the 10am–2pm window on 26 January. Framed work must be wired and ready to hang, and each piece is insured to a maximum of $2,500. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free ($35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 48th Walyalup Fremantle Arts Centre Print Award
item.description: The Walyalup Fremantle Arts Centre Print Award returns for its 48th edition, inviting artists living and working in Australia to enter one work made by any printing process. The brief is print “in all its forms”, the governing clause in the terms is “enter one artwork only, using any printing process”, and the arts centre names “cross-disciplinary artists” among those it wants — and the arts centre’s own call-for-entries release enumerates processes it says entries “may include, but are not limited to”: “etching, lino and woodcut, screen and digital printing, textile-based processes, artist books, 3D and other innovative printmaking practices”. Photography is named on none of the five published surfaces and excluded on none of them either, so a photographic or alternative-process print — a pigment or digital print, photogravure, cyanotype, screenprint — enters under “digital printing” and under the governing clause; the centre of gravity is printmaking, and the award describes itself that way. One artwork per artist, made no earlier than 1 January 2025, with works in multiple parts counted as a single work. Entries close at 5pm AWST on 11 January 2027 — the terms and the FAQ both state that time, the call page gives only the date. A judging panel of three industry professionals, not yet named, selects the exhibition; entrants are notified by 3 March 2027, selected work is delivered by 22 March, winners are announced at the opening on 29 April 2027 and the show runs at the arts centre from 1 May to 1 August 2027. The award is acquisitive — the A$20,000 main prize is supported by the City of Fremantle — and every exhibited work must be available for sale, with a 35% commission plus GST on anything sold, so set the sale price on the entry form carefully. Artists pay the freight to Fremantle; WFAC pays the return freight and insures selected work in its keeping until 9 August 2027. Entry is A$50 including GST and non-refundable, and the form takes up to three JPEG images of the single work (longest side 800px minimum, 5 MB maximum) plus a 100-word biography, a 100-word artist statement and 150 words on the work and its installation. The age bar is 16 or older, but the reference date differs by surface: the terms and the FAQ both say “as at 1 January 2025” while the entry form’s date-of-birth note says “must be 16 years or older as at 1 June 2025” — ask the arts centre if you were born between those two dates. One further exclusion sits only in the FAQ: casual City of Fremantle staff may enter, but permanent and permanent part-time employees of the City may not. — Deadline: January 11, 2027. Fee: A$50. Prize: A$20,000 acquisitive + A$5,000 First Nations Print Award + A$5,000 Young Emerging Print Prize + Exhibition.

item.title: Rawhead Issue 05 — Visual Art
item.description: Rawhead, the online journal of poetry, fiction, nonfiction and visual art, has opened Visual Art and Visual Hybrid submissions for Issue 05 (Spring 2028) ahead of its written genres: the page states “Submissions of Visual Art and Visual Hybrid Work are now open for: Rawhead: Issue 05 (Spring 2028)”, while “submissions for all genres will open for Issue 05 from January 1 through March 1, 2028” — so photographers can send work now, and the issue's own stated window closes on 1 March 2028. The journal is explicit that it is not a horror publication: it wants “work that unsettles through emotional depth, sharp craft, and surprising clarity”, and frames the arts as “a form of resistance against monsters, in whatever shape they take.” Photography is named first among the accepted media — “submit 3 to 10 pieces in any medium — illustration, photography, digital collage, mixed media, painting, sculpture”, uploaded at a minimum of 1500px as .jpg, .png or .tiff. The visual art editor, Caressa Layne, asks for “art that explores the delicate threshold between fear and beauty … not looking for horror or gore, but rather artwork that dances along the edges of heightened emotion”, naming Louise Bourgeois, Francis Bacon, Man Ray, Joseba Eskubi, Anna Weyant and Jinyoung Yu as touchstones. Submitting is free — the journal is “committed to always offering free submissions to all writers and artists” — and the only charges are optional expedited-response tiers on Submittable ($10 and $5 for a decision within two weeks, $15 for a 72-business-hour reply), with an email route offered if Submittable itself is a barrier. One artist and one writer from each standard issue receive a $100 Editor's Spotlight award. AI work is refused outright: “we do not accept AI-generated content. Submissions must be original, human-made, and free of AI assistance.” Simultaneous submissions are accepted, and previously published work is welcome if rights have reverted and six months have passed. Response time is 3–6 months. The journal names a long list of backgrounds it actively seeks — BIPOC and Indigenous creators, refugees and diaspora communities, LGBTQIA2S+, disabled and neurodivergent artists, incarcerated and formerly incarcerated people, elder creators and rural or underserved areas — and takes First Serial, non-exclusive reprint, electronic, archival and non-exclusive anthology rights, with authors retaining everything else. — Deadline: March 1, 2028. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + $100.

item.title: Wilderness · Collect Art
item.description: Collect Art, the Tbilisi-based independent art magazine, is calling for work for an online exhibition and special print edition on the theme of WILDERNESS — “not just a place on a map. It is a state of being — raw, untamed, unfiltered, and free from control.” The organiser wants “works exploring Wilderness in all its forms — from untamed landscapes, natural forces, forests, deserts, oceans and mountains to themes of human-nature relationships, ecological fragility and resilience, solitude, survival, freedom, animal instinct, the feral and primitive, inner wilderness, bodies as landscapes, mythological wilds, and the edge between civilization and chaos,” read “literal, symbolic, emotional, political or deeply personal.” Photography is named in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing, collage, installation, illustration, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, assemblage, fibre art, paper art, printmaking, 3D digital art, glass art and metalwork; the call is open to artists worldwide aged 18 and over. Selection buys a month-long online exhibition plus “a 2-6 page spread in both print and digital magazines” carrying a biography, artist statement, interview, website link and 2–10 artworks, a complimentary digital issue promoted on the magazine's channels, and a link to order the printed version; the curatorial team also picks “a few exceptional artists” for its book edition, “101 Contemporary Artists and More…”. THE COST, published in full: there is NO application fee, and a participation fee of €55 is payable only if your work is accepted — so applying costs nothing, and the €55 is what you pay to take the spread and the online show. Submissions go by email and want up to 12 images with each work's title, medium, size and year, a short biography, an artist statement of at least 100 words, and website and social links. No notification date is published. Five sibling calls from the same magazine are open alongside this one at three different prices — Winter Issue (22 November, €35), Reflection (23 November, €25), Darkness (27 November, €55), Solitude and State of the Art (both 28 November, €55 and €25) — and State of the Art is the one that promises its spread to “each participant” rather than to selected artists. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free (€55 if accepted). Prize: Publication + Online exhibition.

item.title: Darkness · Collect Art
item.description: Collect Art, the Tbilisi-based independent art magazine, invites artists to explore darkness “in its many forms — from the psychological and emotional to the physical, symbolic, and poetic,” for an online exhibition and special magazine edition. The organiser's framing: “Darkness is more than the absence of light. It is a space of mystery, introspection, uncertainty, transformation, and imagination. It can conceal, protect, reveal, or invite us to see beyond what is immediately visible,” and it asks “what can be found in the dark — and what becomes visible only when we stop looking for light?” Work may interpret the theme “through personal experience, atmosphere, symbolism, contrast, or abstraction”. Photography is named in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing, collage, installation, illustration, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, assemblage, fibre art, paper art, printmaking, 3D digital art, glass art and metalwork; the call is open to artists worldwide aged 18 and over. Selection buys a month-long online exhibition plus “a 2-6 page spread in both print and digital magazines” with a biography, artist statement, interview, website link and 2–10 artworks, a complimentary digital issue promoted on the magazine's channels, and a link to order the printed version; the curatorial team also picks “a few exceptional artists” for its book edition, “101 Contemporary Artists and More…”. THE COST, published in full: there is NO application fee, and a participation fee of €55 is payable only if your work is accepted. Submissions go by email and want up to 12 images with each work's title, medium, size and year, a short biography, an artist statement of at least 100 words, and website and social links. No notification date is published. Five sibling calls are open alongside this one at three prices — Winter Issue (22 November, €35), Reflection (23 November, €25), Wilderness (27 November, €55), Solitude and State of the Art (both 28 November, €55 and €25). — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free (€55 if accepted). Prize: Publication + Online exhibition.

item.title: Reflection — Special Edition · Collect Art
item.description: Collect Art, the Tbilisi-based independent art magazine, is calling for work for a special edition on the theme of REFLECTION — “an exploration of how we see, perceive, and understand ourselves and the world around us”, which “can emerge through mirrors, memories, emotions, relationships, nature, or the passage of time.” Beyond the physical image, the organiser says, “reflection invites artists to question identity, examine inner landscapes, and reconsider familiar realities from new perspectives,” and it wants work treating reflection “as a visual, emotional, philosophical, or symbolic experience.” Photography is named in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing, collage, installation, illustration, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, assemblage, fibre art, paper art, printmaking, 3D digital art, glass art and metalwork; the call is open to visual artists worldwide aged 18 and over. What selection buys here is the magazine, not a show: “each selected artist will receive a 2-6 page spread in print and digital magazines including a biography, statement, interview, website, and 2-10 featured artworks”, plus a complimentary digital issue promoted on the magazine's channels and a link to order the printed version; the curatorial team also picks “a few exceptional artists” for its book edition, “101 Contemporary Artists and More…”. Unlike the organiser's Wilderness, Darkness and Solitude calls, this block promises no online exhibition. THE COST, published in full: there is NO application fee, and a participation fee of €25 is payable only if your work is accepted. Submissions go by email and want up to 12 images with each work's title, medium, size and year, a short biography, an artist statement of at least 100 words, and website and social links. No notification date is published. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free (€25 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Winter Issue — Seasonal Edition · Collect Art
item.description: Collect Art, the Tbilisi-based independent art magazine, is reading for its Winter seasonal issue, and this one is open-ended by design: “there is no theme for this edition.” Photography is named in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing, collage, installation, illustration, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, assemblage, fibre art, paper art, printmaking, 3D digital art, glass art and metalwork, and the call is open to artists worldwide aged 18 and over — so it is the organiser's one current route for work that does not answer to a theme. What selection buys is the magazine: “each selected artist will receive a 2-6 page spread in both print and digital magazines, featuring a biography, statement, interview, website, and 2-10 selected artworks”, plus a complimentary digital issue promoted on the magazine's channels and a link to order the printed version; the curatorial team also picks “a few exceptional artists” for its book edition, “101 Contemporary Artists and More…”. No online exhibition is promised in this block. THE COST, published in full: there is NO application fee, and a participation fee of €35 is payable only if your work is accepted — a price that sits between the organiser's €25 and €55 calls. Submissions go by email and want up to 12 images with each work's title, medium, size and year, a short biography, an artist statement of at least 100 words, and website and social links. No notification date is published. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free (€35 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Land and Sea: Celebrating Our National Marine Sanctuary · Pajaro Valley Arts
item.description: Pajaro Valley Arts, the Watsonville nonprofit, is running an invitational and juried exhibition FOR PHOTOGRAPHY AND DIGITAL ART ONLY, presented alongside Photo Carmel Month in April 2027, on the Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary — which “spans from Rocky Point in Marin County to Cambria in San Luis Obispo County, reaching 25 miles offshore and inland to the ridges of the Coast Range.” The brief is deliberately wider than a nature show: PVA “invites photographers and digital artists living and/or working in the greater Bay Area to explore this territory in full — its waters, wildlife, working harbors, towns, industry, and people,” and welcomes “images of any subject connected to this region: marine life, coastal landscapes, architecture, industry, and the everyday people who live and work here. The goal is a fuller picture of the sanctuary — not just its natural beauty, but the human life built around it.” The jury is the reason to look twice: Ted Orland and Brian Taylor, with Joan Blackmer and Chad Williams curating. Entry is free and takes up to 5 JPEGs of work new to PVA, submitted through the gallery's own entry form (JPEGs at no more than 300 dpi and 6” in any direction, filenames as surname plus title); a hard-copy form is available on request. The exhibition runs 23 March – 2 May 2027 with a reception on Saturday 27 March, 1–3pm, and both invited and open-call artists are hung. THE COSTS, published in full: there is no application fee, but “upon acceptance/selection into the exhibit, there is a $35.00 participation fee for each artist, to be paid with the submittal of the loan agreement” — PVA says it “helps offset exhibit expenses” and that “some participation sponsorships may be available”, so ask if the fee is a barrier. Sales commission is 30% for PVA members and 50% for non-members, and you must be a member in good standing through 2 May 2027 to get the lower rate. TWO PRACTICAL LIMITS: PVA is “unable to accept artwork through the mail for this exhibit” — artists or their representatives deliver in person to Watsonville on 15 March, 10am–2pm — and framed work is capped at 36 inches wide, wired and ready to hang, insured to a maximum of $2,500 per piece. Artists are notified on 22 February 2027, with loan forms and artist statements due 5 March. — Deadline: February 16, 2027. Fee: Free ($35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Solitude · Collect Art
item.description: Collect Art, the Tbilisi-based independent art magazine, is calling for work for a curated online exhibition and special print edition on the theme of SOLITUDE — “the quiet space between self and world — the moments when noise falls away and only presence remains.” The organiser is specific about what it wants to see: “visual interpretations of solitude — whether that means an empty room at dusk, a figure turned inward, a landscape without human trace, or the invisible solitude we carry even in a crowd,” and sets the theme against its own questions: “In a world obsessed with connection, visibility, and constant noise, what does it mean to be alone? Is solitude loneliness, or is it freedom? Is it exile, or is it return?” Photography is named in the eligible-media list, alongside painting, drawing, collage, installation, illustration, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, assemblage, fibre art, paper art, printmaking, 3D digital art, glass art and metalwork; the call is open to artists worldwide aged 18 and over. What selection buys, in the organiser's own words: a month-long online exhibition plus “a 2-6 page spread in both print and digital magazines” carrying a biography, artist statement, interview, website link and 2–10 featured artworks, a complimentary digital issue promoted on the magazine's site and social channels, and a link to order the printed version. The curatorial team also picks “a few exceptional artists” for its forthcoming book edition, “101 Contemporary Artists and More…”. The cost structure matters and is published in full: there is NO application fee, and a participation fee of €55 is payable only if your work is accepted — so applying costs nothing, and the €55 is what you pay to take the magazine spread and the online show. Submissions go by email and want up to 12 images with the work's title, medium, size and year, a short biography, an artist statement of at least 100 words, and website and social links. No notification date is published. Five sibling calls from the same magazine are open alongside this one, at three different prices — Winter Issue (22 November 2026, €35 if accepted), Reflection (23 November 2026, €25 if accepted), Darkness and Wilderness (27 November 2026, €55 each if accepted) and State of the Art (28 November 2026, €25 if accepted). One difference is worth reading before you choose: State of the Art promises its spread to “each participant”, while this call promises it to “selected artists”. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: Free (€55 if accepted). Prize: Publication + Online exhibition.

item.title: Make it Midwest: A Regional Exhibition · Fishers Art Center
item.description: Fishers Art Center, the new public art centre inside the Fishers Arts & Municipal Complex outside Indianapolis — free to visit, and programmed and managed by the 90-year-old Indy Art Center — is calling for entries to a juried regional exhibition of contemporary Midwest makers. The call is explicitly open to every medium: "The Fishers Art Center is calling for entries for artists in any medium 18 or older living in the Midwest", and again, "Artists working in any media or processes are eligible for entry. The intention of this exhibition is to feature works in a variety of media ranging from traditional processes to contemporary and new media processes" — so photography, analog and digital alike, is in scope. Eligibility is by residence: artists currently working in Indiana, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan, Kentucky, Missouri, Iowa, Wisconsin, Kansas or Nebraska, aged 18 or over. Work must have been made in the last two years and must not have been shown at the Art Center before; collaborative works between artists are eligible; nothing may weigh more than 250 pounds or measure more than 10 feet in any direction, and installation artists are asked to make contact before applying. Entry is $35 for two pieces with $5 for each additional piece, up to a maximum of fifteen. Four awards are given: Best in Show $300, Best in 2D $150, Best in 3D $150 and Curator's Choice $150. Accepted work hangs in the Art Center's galleries, which are free and open to the public, from 12 February to 11 April 2027, with a reception on opening night from 6 to 8pm; the Art Center takes a 35% commission on any sales and work may also be entered not for sale. The schedule the organiser publishes runs: applications close 16 December 2026, acceptance notifications by end of day 17 December, artwork drop-off 4–31 January 2027, installation 1–11 February, exhibition 12 February to 11 April, pick-up 12–16 April. Artists hand-deliver or pay shipping and insurance both ways, and work must arrive in a reusable container. Entry is through the CaFÉ / Creative West portal. The Art Center names no juror on either surface, though the Curator's Choice award implies one; it also runs a separate year-round proposal route for solo and group exhibitions by email, reviewed on a rolling basis. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: $35 for 2 works, $5 each additional. Prize: $300/$150/$150/$150 + Exhibition.

item.title: Curatorial Research Trips — January–June 2027 · Fluxus Art Projects
item.description: Fluxus Art Projects funds work that moves between the two countries it exists to connect: it supports projects promoting the contemporary French art scene in the UK and the contemporary British art scene in France, and it runs its own call for applications twice a year. This round covers projects taking place between January and June 2027 and closes at midnight on Tuesday 24 November 2026. The call has two separate streams and the difference matters before you start an application. Exhibition projects are funded between £1,000 and £10,000, but the fund states that applications must be submitted by the organising institution or association and not by the artists themselves — eligible applicants there are non-profit art centres, museums, cultural institutions, research centres, online projects and artists' publications — so an individual artist cannot apply to that stream. Curatorial research trips work the other way round: applications must be made directly by the curators, and the grant is a flat £1,000 per trip. The curatorial criteria are specific. You must be French or resident in France for at least five years, or British or resident in the UK for at least five years; you need a minimum of three years of professional experience, or evidence of significant professional practice within an art organisation or as an independent curator in the field of contemporary art; and if you are attached to an institution you must supply its authorisation to travel for the research you are proposing. Fluxus describes its field as visual arts in the broadest sense across all disciplines, and the curatorial criteria name contemporary art, so a photography curator is in scope; the fund says it will prioritise innovative practices and the production of new works. The call page names no application fee at any point. Applications go through a Google Form and must be written in English, and the fund asks you to send a confirmation email to its own address as well as submitting the form. Fluxus Art Projects is a Franco-British fund supported by the Institut français du Royaume-Uni, the British Council, Arts Council England, Creative Scotland and the French Ministry of Culture; it also runs the Magnetic artist residencies in tandem pairs of a French region with a UK nation, and prizes at Frieze London and Art Basel Paris, all of which are closed at the time of writing. Applications are selected by the fund's standing Artistic Committee, named on its About page: Hélène Nguyen-Ban as chair, Margot Heller of the South London Gallery, Caroline Bourgeois of the Bourse du Commerce, Wells Fray-Smith of the Barbican, Daria de Beauvais of the Palais de Tokyo, Martin Clark of Camden Art Centre, Nicolas Gausserand of the musées d'Orsay and the Orangerie, and Edward Gillman of Chisenhale Gallery, alongside representatives of the public partners. The fund publishes no notification date for this round. — Deadline: November 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 research grant.

item.title: Premier Prix photographique du Musée Postal
item.description: The first photography prize created by the Musée Postal in Paris — the museum of La Poste, founded in 1946, a Musée de France and a corporate museum holding a photographic collection of some 250,000 documents — launched for the Bicentenary of Photography. It funds the production of one new photographic project on La Poste today, with a grant of €15,000 (TTC) paid directly to the artist. The brief is open as to approach and tight as to subject: the project must look at the contemporary postal world in its human, material and/or immaterial dimensions, must continue the applicant's existing artistic practice, and must offer an original, contemporary view. The museum names mobility and flows, ecological transformation, technological innovation, territorial presence, and trades and social questions as examples of what a project might address, and states that every photographic approach is welcome — documentary, reportage, fine-art and experimental alike. Applications are open only to professional photographers, with no age limit, resident in France (metropolitan or overseas) and able to prove professional status: an URSSAF attestation, artiste-auteur status, a Kbis extract or a production-company attestation are all accepted as proof. There is no entry fee. The dossier goes by email as a PDF attachment of no more than 10 MB — the règlement recommends, but does not require, that it be a single file — and must contain an illustrated artistic portfolio of at most six pages covering the applicant's practice and earlier work, a statement of intent of at most two pages with a 500-character summary, a CV or account of the applicant's path with full contact details and a copy of a valid ID, and the proof of professional status; anything illegible, incomplete or late is ruled inadmissible without being read. Selection runs in two stages — the jury reads every dossier and preselects a number of applicants by 15 December 2026, then those applicants present their project to the jury in person at the museum (or remotely if necessary) on 6 January 2027, after which the winner is chosen and told by email, and possibly by telephone, at the end of the deliberation. The jury is named in full and is substantial: it includes the director of the agency Signatures, the museum's own director, a professor of art history at the Beaux-arts de Paris, the cultural lead at Magnum Photos, and an artist teaching at the ENSP in Arles. Beyond the money, a selection of signed and numbered prints from the winning project enters the museum's collection — their production is paid for and carried out by La Fabrique de l'image, the prize's partner laboratory in Meysse, Ardèche — and the winner gets privileged access and support within the La Poste group to make the work. Two conditions are worth reading before applying: the règlement requires the applicant to state explicitly in the project description and/or statement of intent whether any image or video is generated or transformed with an AI tool, naming the tools and the extent of their use, with failure to disclose grounds for disqualification even after the winner has been named; and payment of the grant is conditional on signing a copyright assignment contract with the museum covering the works produced, which sets out the rights assigned, their duration and territory, and a non-exclusive assignment of reproduction and representation rights. The museum reserves the right not to award the prize if it judges the dossiers insufficient, and may adjust the calendar, announcing any change on its own website. Production of the series runs February–June 2027 and the prints are made in July 2027. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €15,000 production grant.

item.title: Expressions West 2027 · Coos Art Museum
item.description: The 2027 edition of Coos Art Museum's annual regional juried exhibition, open to artists living in thirteen western states — Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. Coos Art Museum is the only art museum on the Oregon Coast, housed in Coos Bay's 1936 Art Deco former post office, and Expressions West is its survey of what is being made across the American West — no theme, work judged on its own terms. Photography is an explicitly eligible medium alongside painting, drawing, hand-pulled prints, mixed media, fiber and textiles, small sculpture, glass, turned and carved wood, jewellery and furniture; prints must be framed and ready for hanging and no work may exceed 48 inches in any direction including the frame. Read the exclusions before you pay: digital artwork, AI artwork, video, film, audio and giclée prints are all ineligible, so an inkjet-printed photograph does not qualify and the call wants a photographic print made another way. The juror for 2027 is Daemian Hawthorn, an artist working across drawing, painting and welded metal sculpture. Awards are $1,000 for First Place, $750 for Second and $250 for Third. Up to three works may be submitted, with five images allowed per artwork; the fee is $35 for the first submission and $10 each for the second and third. The museum states the schedule in full: submissions close 6 December 2026, acceptance or rejection is notified on 22 December 2026, accepted artwork must reach the museum by 23 January 2027, the opening reception is 6 February 2027, and work is retrieved in person on 23–24 April 2027 or returned by courier on 24 April. Artwork is insured from arrival until return. Artists are responsible for getting work back: you may arrange and pay for your own return shipping, or ask the museum to coordinate it and be charged the shipping costs plus a $30 handling fee. Work made under an instructor's supervision is not eligible, and entries must be original in concept, composition and execution. Work must have been made in the last two years (2024–2026), must not have been shown at Coos Art Museum before, and if it is part of a series the entered piece has to be distinguishable from your others. Sales are the artist's own: the museum takes no commission and processes no transactions, so you set the price and deal with the buyer directly. One caution about the date — the museum's own Important Dates block closes submissions on 6 December 2026, while the CaFE record's machine deadline field reads 23:59:59 Pacific on 9 December. Treat 6 December as the date that binds. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: $35 first work + $10 each additional (up to 3). Prize: $1,000 / $750 / $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: Being Seen 2027 · TAG/The Artists Gallery
item.description: A regional juried exhibition at TAG/The Artists Gallery, an artist-run gallery at 501 N Market Street in Frederick, Maryland, hung in the gallery itself from 5 to 28 March 2027 with a reception on 6 March, 5–8 pm. The gallery's premise for the show: "If a tree falls in a forest, does it make a sound? It does only if there is an observer. Art also needs an observer to truly Be Seen because art is not complete until it connects with the heart and mind of the viewer." The juror is Florencio Lennox (Lenny) Campello — an artist, curator, critic and author of 100 Artists of Washington, DC, who has juried or curated over 200 fine art shows and recently assembled the Women Artists of the DMV survey across twenty venues in the capital region. Photographs in both analog and digital formats are explicitly eligible, alongside original paintings, drawings, prints, mixed media including digital collage and manipulations, and sculpture; work must have been made in the last three years, must not have been shown at TAG before, and no reproductions of pre-existing artwork or video are accepted. Awards, chosen by the juror, are $500 First Prize, $250 Second, $125 Third and three Honorable Mentions of $50 each. The eligibility bar is tight and worth reading twice: open to artists 18 and over living in Maryland, DC, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania or Delaware, within easy driving distance of Frederick, and not currently represented by TAG. That driving-distance clause is enforced by the logistics rather than by a map — there is no shipping option in either direction, and accepted work must be hand-delivered to the gallery on 28 February or 1 March 2027 (2–6 pm) and collected on 28 or 29 March, with $5 a day charged for storage after that and disposal possible after thirty days. All wall-hung work including the frame must stay within 48 inches in any direction and 6 inches deep, under 30 lbs, framed and ready to hang with wire or a cleat — no sawtooth hangers. All work must be for sale with no price-on-request, and the gallery takes 30% commission. Judging runs 13–24 January 2027 and the gallery aims to notify every applicant by 29 January. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: $35 first work + $5 each additional (up to 3). Prize: $500 / $250 / $125 + three $50 honorable mentions + Exhibition.

item.title: Dream of Home Away · Van Der Plas Gallery
item.description: The next cycle of Van Der Plas Gallery's year-round Open Call Program, for a group exhibition titled Dream of Home Away at the gallery's Lower East Side space at 156 Orchard Street, on view 12–25 February 2027 with an opening reception on 12 February, 6–8 pm. Founded in New York City in the 1980s, the gallery shows emerging and established contemporary artists with a focus on downtown culture, outsider art, street art, painting, sculpture and experimental practices, and photography is named explicitly among the media it wants — alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media, digital art and experimental practices. The brief is not thematic in any strict sense: the gallery says it looks for "originality, conceptual clarity, and a strong artistic vision" and work that reflects the diversity of contemporary practice, and the exhibition is meant to bring together different practices from artists at different career stages inside a professional gallery setting. Applying is open to artists at any stage, internationally, with no age or residence bar: $35 buys the review of up to four artworks (JPG), plus installation images for any framed or otherwise applicable work, an artist bio and an artist statement of 100–200 words each. Submissions are read on a rolling basis by the gallery's own curatorial team, selection is not guaranteed, and work submitted now is considered for Dream of Home Away first and then stays under consideration for later exhibitions in the programme; artists may apply again at any time and each submission is read independently. Selected artists are contacted directly by email, with no published notification date. The commercial terms are worth knowing before you pay: the gallery states the $35 covers submission review, administrative coordination, exhibition planning and the running costs of a physical gallery; all shipping, delivery and return arrangements and their costs fall on the artist, including for international applicants; every accepted work must be available for sale for the run of the show, with pricing agreed with the gallery after acceptance, and work not for sale may be declined or excluded; and the framing specification is enforced — work on paper must be framed, with a recommended minimum two-inch mat, a museum-style frame in natural wood, black or whitewashed finish and plexiglass rather than glass, and work that does not meet it "may be excluded from the exhibition, even after delivery". The gallery will frame to spec for an additional fee on request. The binding document is a Terms and Conditions PDF linked from the call page, last updated 25 October 2026, and it carries five things the page itself does not: sales made during or as a result of the exhibition are split 50% artist / 50% gallery; submitted work must not exceed 48 by 60 inches, and anything over 36 by 48 inches has to be shipped unstretched; artists must supply a prepaid return shipping label and email a copy to the gallery; unsold work left past the collection date incurs a $250 storage fee after three days and may be donated or discarded after a month, with no compensation; and every applicant, selected or not, is told the outcome in the first week of January. The same document sets no age, residence or AI condition. — Deadline: January 22, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: PHODAR Biennial 14 — Traces Remain · PHODAR Foundation
item.description: The 14th edition of the PHODAR Biennial, Bulgaria's oldest international photography competition — running since 1999 and organised by the PHODAR Foundation in Sofia, with the Sofia Municipality Culture Programme and exhibitions historically staged at the National Gallery — asks for a coherent series on the theme "Traces Remain". The title is borrowed from the novel by the Bulgarian writer Pavel Vezhinov, and the brief runs through Susan Sontag's On Photography: the photograph as a trace of reality, physically connected to what once stood before the lens, and at the same time a reminder of transience. The organisers' questions are the interesting part — "How do we read the traces of the past in the present? What do abandoned spaces, altered landscapes, family archives and marks on the human body reveal? Which traces do we deliberately preserve, and which do we try to erase? Can a photograph sustain a memory when its story has already been lost?" — and they say the theme is open to any genre that answers them, documentary, portraiture or conceptual alike, including work on social conflict, generational relationships and the transformation of surroundings. Entry is free and there are two sections, each author choosing one: the Grand Prize section and Debut, the latter reserved for authors at the beginning of a career without serious national or international achievements yet. A separate Award for Humanistic Photography goes to one author regardless of section. Submissions are a series or photo essay of 8 to 20 images from an ongoing or completed project, JPEG, minimum 3000 pixels on the longest side at 300 DPI, numbered in the order you want them read; the work has to have been made on or after 1 January 2025, with an exception for long-term projects begun earlier and continued since. Stock photography is not accepted, one series per author, and collaborative series by two or more photographers are explicitly welcome. Entry is open to professional and amateur photographers over 18 with no restriction on country of origin or citizenship. Finalists' prints are produced and mounted at the Foundation's expense for the PHODAR Awards exhibition in Sofia, the prints staying with the Foundation; copyright remains with the photographer throughout, and selected authors are shown in an online winners gallery and published in the edition photobook. Past award winners the Foundation names include Donald Weber (VII Photo Agency) and Mila Teshaieva. Note one disagreement between the organiser's own surfaces: the rules page states a deadline of 1 January 2027 while the submission form at entry.phodar.net prints "DEADLINE IS 31.12.2026" — the earlier, form-stated date is the one to work to, and the rules add that the Foundation may extend without notice. Prizes are paid in euros once the Foundation has received the award funding, with any international payment or conversion charges deducted from the prize. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €2,000 Grand Prize + €600 Debut Award + €600 Humanistic Photography Award + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Visual Art Open Prize 2027
item.description: The 12th edition of the Visual Art Open, a UK-based international art award with a £10,000 prize fund and a dedicated Photography & Digital Art category alongside Painting, Sculpture, Drawing & Illustration, Mixed Media/Collage/Printmaking, Student Artist and Art Educator. The overall winner takes £2,000 in cash, a solo exhibition at a London venue, a place in the London finalists' show at the Minster Building, a dedicated article on their practice, and a year of Visual Artists Association premium membership with its mentorship and Momentum business-development programmes. Each category winner receives £250, the same VAA membership and course, a place in the finalists' exhibition, an article and extra online promotion. All finalists are invited to exhibit in central London and receive a certificate; every entrant is put forward for promotion across the VAA's social channels and its 60,000-subscriber mailing list. Entry is open worldwide to artists at every career stage, from first-time entrants to established practitioners, and the organisers make a point of discounted rates for students and art educators, which stay fixed across the whole entry period. Work is submitted as JPEG or PNG images up to 5MB, up to five per entry, and the number of works has to be chosen before checkout because the price changes with it. Judging is by a panel drawn from commercial galleries, museums, art media and academia — recent panels have included the creative director of Mall Galleries, the senior fair manager of The Other Art Fair, and the critic Tabish Khan — though the organisers have not yet published the panel under the 2027 label. The prize is funded by entry fees, donations, art sales, advertising and sponsorship rather than by Arts Council money, and entries cannot be refunded once submitted. Early-bird pricing runs to 17 December 2026; standard pricing applies from 18 December 2026 until the entry period closes on 25 March 2027. The terms page adds bars and costs the entry pages never mention: entry is open from age 14, with written authorisation from a legal guardian for anyone under 18; work must have been made within the last three years and must not already have been sold; and a 40% commission is taken on anything that sells through the VAO exhibition. AI work is barred outright — the rules require that every submission be “created manually and entirely by the artist”, and state that “AI-generated or AI-assisted artwork is not eligible for entry”. One number is worth doing yourself: of the advertised £10,000 fund the published cash is £3,750 — £2,000 to the overall winner and £250 to each of the seven category winners — with the balance made up of the VAA memberships, courses, London exhibition places and certificates listed above. — Deadline: March 25, 2027. Fee: £15–£55 early bird (1–5 works), £20–£60 from 18 Dec; £10–£35 student/educator. Prize: £10,000 fund — £2,000 + solo exhibition in London.

item.title: Amsterdam Artist Showcase — February 2027 · Arrival Gallery
item.description: Arrival Gallery's three-day group showcase in Amsterdam, 12 to 14 February 2027, at Zesde Vogelstraat 40 in the city's west. The gallery takes submissions from painters, photographers, sculptors, illustrators, textile, mixed-media and digital artists, and describes itself as working with emerging, independent and mid-career practitioners. Photographic, moving-image and screen-based work is explicitly catered for: alongside hung physical work, Arrival presents digital pieces through curated display screens, digital exhibition formats, online artist features and city activations, which makes the digital route a realistic option for a photographer who does not want to ship and frame prints. Submitting work for review is free and there is no entry fee. The cost comes after selection, and Arrival publishes the floors rather than hiding them: the Digital Showcase route starts from £65 and the Physical Showcase route from £165, with the full format, timeline and preparation details sent to selected artists before they confirm a place. Applicants pick their preferred route — digital, physical or featured — when they submit, or ask the gallery to recommend one. Places are sold from a limited release, so the gallery's own framing is that confirmation secures a slot from the current batch rather than that selection alone guarantees a wall. Anyone considering this should read it for what it is: a paid-participation showcase, free to enter, where the real decision comes once a price is quoted. — Deadline: January 28, 2027. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: København Noir — Din By i Sort-Hvid · Copenhagen Photo Festival
item.description: A free black-and-white photo hunt through Copenhagen's old working-class districts, run by Copenhagen Photo Festival with Københavns Museum, CEWE and a group of Copenhagen photographers under the city's Vinter i København programme. Nine archive photographs from the museum's collection have been installed outdoors on the streets and squares of Nørrebro, Vesterbro and Nordvest — each one at the spot where it was originally taken. The task is to find them, one or two or all nine, and submit your own black-and-white pictures made in the area around them. The festival's framing is unapologetically atmospheric: a tribute to contrast, to the aesthetics of decay and renewal, to street life and dusk, to "that Copenhagen which is rarely captured", and to the time of year Danes associate with endless darkness — the page opens with Henrik Nordbrandt's line that the year has sixteen months, "November, December, January... November, November, November, November". Street photography in black and white is what the organisers say they are after, worked alone or with others. Entry is free and every submitted photograph is automatically in the running to be exhibited at Absalon on 22 November, the day the project culminates at the festival's off-season photo market. Three guided photo walks with the photographers Christopher 'Flip' Egeberg, Jón Bjarni Hjartarson and Christine Lorenzen run alongside the hunt, offering black-and-white street technique to anyone who wants it. The entry terms, which live on the CEWE contest platform rather than on the festival's own page, restrict entry to people resident in Copenhagen ("Deltagelsesberettigede er fysiske personer, som har bopæl i København"), and the work has to be made around the nine specific locations, so this is for people who live in the city and are in it before 3 November; entrants under 18 confirm that a parent or guardian has read the terms and consents. The same terms set out what is actually awarded: the contest runs in nine categories, one per location, with a maximum of one photograph per category; a specialist jury picks 27 winning images (three per location) for the Absalon show and ranks the best three, where first prize is CEWE photo products worth DKK 2,000, second is Christopher 'Flip' Egeberg's photobook about the street artist SPYO, given by Københavns Museum, and third is a voucher for two tickets to Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027. Winners are told by email, with no notification date published, and nothing is posted out — prizes are handed over at Absalon on 22 November or collected afterwards from the festival office. Images made wholly by computer or by artificial intelligence are barred and will be excluded, retouching that adds or removes content is not allowed, and the extent of any editing has to be stated in the image description. The festival calls it a taste of next year's edition, when the hunt returns at larger scale as Copenhagen Photo Festival moves from June to November. — Deadline: November 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: DKK 2,000 in CEWE products + Exhibition at Absalon, 22 November.

item.title: 1839 Awards Art of Photography Contest
item.description: The 2026 edition of the 1839 Awards' Art of Photography Contest, which the organiser frames as celebrating "the creativity, vision, and distinctive perspectives that make photography an art form, across every genre". It takes over from the Art of Storytelling Contest, whose own page is still up but carries the finished 2025 edition (8 September 2025 to 14 January 2026); the site now lists three annual contests: Photographer of the Year, Art of Photography and Color Photography. MIND THE TWO DEADLINES.
